failures.cause: The durable fixture called ordinary nonblocking abort_all_tasks then injected before an existing exact cleanup owner completed.
failures.change: Wait on pending_turn_cleanup with its live generation result, then retain the original injection and durability checks.

failures.cause: The test inspected a transient empty reference baseline after spawning the initial prompt, which can already rebuild that baseline.
failures.change: Use existing pause_next_startup_before_delivery after child registration and before initial prompt delivery; keep all original history, selected roots and None baseline assertions, then release and assert the delivered thread identity.

failures.cause: The pinned tracing-core single-dispatch optimization may cache never-interest when another thread first registers the static callsite without a scoped subscriber. Exact pinned native reproducer demonstrates this mechanism; complete Windows reproduction awaits CI.
failures.change: Retain a second uninstalled NoSubscriber Dispatch during this scoped capture test; preserve all original nested-span and readiness assertions. No dependency or production tracing change.

failures.cause: The goal idle callback attempted immediate atomic turn admission while its caller still owned the terminalization cleanup fence; rejection had no later wake-up. Static lifecycle analysis matches the missing final goal request. Full new-code execution awaits CI.
failures.change: Defer only this goal runtime outside the callback, track exact thread Arc and generation, deduplicate unfinished waits, weakly retain the runtime, wait for the original completion, then recheck loaded Arc, current goal, deferral and unchanged atomic admission. Do not replay global idle lifecycle or weaken the fence.

failures.cause: Pinned Nucleo clears should_notify before trying the worker lock; after a lock timeout, its worker can read false and finish before tick stores true. The resulting running=true can lack a completion callback. Once the one-shot timer and WalkComplete have been consumed, the old matcher loop never ticks again. This is a proven source-level race, not a claim that the Windows log reveals its unique scheduling cause.
failures.change: Rearm the existing 10ms timer while tick reports running, and disable the timer with never() when idle. Preserve the original 600-file streaming test and its five-second bound.

new_behavior_tests.name: matcher_completes_without_a_worker_notification
new_behavior_tests.behavior: Prime real Nucleo with an empty pattern until idle, inject one existing temporary file without further tick/reparse, intentionally replace notify with a no-op, and send only WalkComplete. Its first non-canceled tick must report running; completion must then arrive without another callback. Shutdown and join occur before assertions, followed by exact scanned/matched counts and filename checks.

findings: Exact captured completion waits run outside the lifecycle callback; standard Mutex guards do not cross await.
Weak runtime and thread references avoid a registry/JoinHandle strong-reference cycle.
After readiness the path rereads the current manager Arc, goal state permit, deferral and goal; original atomic turn admission remains authoritative.
No global lifecycle replay or cleanup fence weakening.
limits: Static review only, no workspace compile or Windows execution.
Dropping JoinHandle detaches; this is not a real-time cancellation guarantee. The wait has weak ownership and the original session-termination exit.

scope: exact pinned Nucleo lib.rs and worker.rs
findings: Rearming only while running closes the callback-loss gap without polling when idle.
The real matcher regression primes Fresh/Unchanged before injection, so the first post-injection tick starts work and reports running.
No extra query/reparse or tick can accidentally consume the deterministic test setup.
The original timeout and streaming assertion remain unchanged; shutdown and join precede the final assertion.
